# Baruch Chapter 1 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Baruch 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/BAR_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1** These are the words of the book that Baruch son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, son of Zedekiah, son of Hasadiah, son of Hilkiah, wrote in Babylon,

**2** in the fifth year, on the seventh day of the month, at the time when the Chaldeans captured Jerusalem and burned it with fire.

**3** And Baruch read the words of this book aloud to Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and to all the people who came to hear the book read —

**4** to the nobles and the sons of kings, to the elders, and to all the people, both small and great, all those who lived in Babylon by the River Sud.

**5** Then they wept and fasted and prayed before the Lord.

**6** And they collected money, each as much as he was able to give,

**7** and sent it to Jerusalem, to the priest Jehoiakim son of Hilkiah son of Shallum, and to the priests and to all the people who were with him in Jerusalem.

**8** This was at the time when Jehoiakim received the vessels of the house of the Lord that had been carried away from the temple — to bring them back to the land of Judah on the tenth day of Sivan — the silver vessels which Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, had made,

**9** after King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon had carried away Jeconiah and the princes and the prisoners and the warriors and the people of the land from Jerusalem and brought them to Babylon.

**10** They said: Here we send you money; use the money to buy burnt offerings and sin offerings and frankincense, and prepare grain offerings, and offer them all on the altar of the Lord our God.

**11** And pray for the life of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon and for the life of his son Belshazzar, that their days upon earth may be like the days of heaven.

**12** And the Lord will give us strength and light our eyes, and we shall live under the protection of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon and under the protection of his son Belshazzar, and we shall serve them for many days and find favor in their sight.

**13** Pray also to the Lord our God on our behalf, for we have sinned against the Lord our God, and his anger and his wrath have not turned away from us to this very day.

**14** You shall read aloud this book which we have sent to you, to make confession in the house of the Lord on the feast day and throughout the days of the appointed seasons.

**15** And you shall say: Righteousness belongs to the Lord our God, but to us belongs open shame, as it is this day — to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem,

**16** to our kings and our princes, to our priests and our prophets and to our ancestors —

**17** because we sinned before the Lord our God.

**18** We disobeyed him; we did not listen to the voice of the Lord our God or walk in the commandments that the Lord set before us.

**19** From the day when the Lord brought our ancestors out of the land of Egypt until this present day, we have been disobedient to the Lord our God; we have been careless and have not heeded his voice.

**20** Therefore the evils and the curse that the Lord decreed through his servant Moses — on the day when he brought our ancestors out of the land of Egypt to give us a land flowing with milk and honey — have clung to us to this very day.

**21** We did not listen to the voice of the Lord our God in keeping with all the words of the prophets whom he sent to us;

**22** but each of us followed the intentions of his own wicked heart, serving other gods and doing what is evil in the sight of the Lord our God.

---
*LOGOS notes: v.4 "nobles" for the Greek dynasts/powerful men; "River Sud" retained as proper name though not certainly identified. v.14 the public reading context mirrors Nehemiah 8. v.20 "clung to us" preserves the adhesion metaphor of the Greek.*
